author: blu
body: The generated program is assembled with SeLines, one expression per line, rather than as a here-string. Two lines interpolate: the header byte list and the seed length. Everything else is a literal, and those literals are full of double quotes because they are Codex source -- which is exactly what the old ps-quote could not emit, since it wrapped literals in double quotes and escaped nothing.

author: blu
body: The generated script names -OutFile in full where the one it replaces wrote -Out. PowerShell binds that by unambiguous prefix and both reach the same parameter, but the prefix stops being unambiguous the day test-run gains a second parameter starting with Out.
